hints: Focus on what heterogeneous really means, a catalyst in a different physical state from the reactants, usually a solid with gaseous reactants.
Recall the Haber process for ammonia and the Contact process for sulfuric acid, both use a solid catalyst with all gaseous reactants.
Think about the catalytic converter in cars, where solid platinum and rhodium clean up gaseous NO and CO, then decide if all three fit.
walkthrough:
**Recall the heterogeneous test**

Think side by side with me. Homogeneous means same state, heterogeneous means different state.

Rule to use:
$$\text{heterogeneous if catalyst (s) } \neq \text{ reactants (g or aq)}$$

**Check reaction 1, the Haber process**

All reactants and products are gases, but the iron catalyst is a solid. That is different states, so it is heterogeneous.

$$\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + 3\text{H}_2(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3(\text{g}) \quad \text{with Fe(s)}$$

**Check reaction 2, the Contact process**

Again all reactants are gases, but vanadium(V) oxide is a solid. That is also different states, so it is heterogeneous.

$$2\text{SO}_2(\text{g}) + \text{O}_2(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3(\text{g}) \quad \text{with V}_2\text{O}_5(\text{s})$$

**Check reaction 3, the catalytic converter**

Both NO and CO are pollutant gases, but the platinum and rhodium catalyst is a solid honeycomb. Gases adsorbing onto a solid surface is classic heterogeneous catalysis.

$$2\text{NO}(\text{g}) + 2\text{CO}(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{N}_2(\text{g}) + 2\text{CO}_2(\text{g}) \quad \text{with Pt/Rh(s)}$$

**Conclude the combination**

Since 1, 2 and 3 all use a solid catalyst with gaseous reactants, all three can use a heterogeneous catalyst.

options.A: Correct and well done. Reactions 1, 2 and 3 are all catalysed heterogeneously by solids: Fe in the Haber process, V2O5 in the Contact process, and Pt/Rh in the catalytic converter for NO and CO.
options.B: Incorrect. This option includes only 1 and 2 and leaves out 3. Students sometimes forget that catalytic converters are also heterogeneous, but gases reacting on solid Pt/Rh is a perfect example.
options.C: Incorrect. This option includes only 2 and 3 and leaves out 1. Students sometimes confuse the Haber iron catalyst, but Fe(s) with N2(g) and H2(g) is definitely heterogeneous.
options.D: Incorrect. This option includes only 1 and leaves out 2 and 3. Students sometimes think only the Haber process uses a solid, but the Contact process and catalytic converter also use solid catalysts with gases.
